decisions.summary: The arm is set with --effort, never CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL; the launcher unsets the variable and records that
decisions.why: The env variable beats frontmatter effort and would break the pinned-checker control (FR-005); --effort is the handoff's preferred mechanism.

decisions.summary: Ad-hoc judging routed to a session-scoped adhoc-judge (opus, effort high) defined by an identical --agents JSON; the prompt names no effort
decisions.why: Implements FR-005 / US2 AS3 (ad-hoc checking or judging at one fixed effort in both arms); any fixed level satisfies it.

decisions.summary: Only task I is launched with --agents; task R's page sessions get EFFORT only (contracts/cli.md page-session and effort-run step 3)
decisions.why: FR-005 and US2 AS3 apply to every run. Page sessions have the Agent tool and their rules allow ad-hoc opus judging, so on task R (the task hypothesis 2 says is most effort-sensitive) ad-hoc judges run at the session effort and the adhoc-judge the briefs would name does not exist. The runner must pass the same --agents JSON (and the briefs carry the same routing instruction).

decisions.summary: If --agents cannot carry effort (P0 a), go straight to the spec's measured unmet branch; a committed agent file was rejected as a permanent agent for a one-off
decisions.why: US2 AS3's unmet branch applies only when the effort is MEASURED to be impossible to set. A defined agent file with effort frontmatter is a documented way to set it, and was rejected for cost and tidiness, which cannot justify dropping a control. Fallback must be an agent file identical across arms (committed before START or placed by the launcher), and the unmet branch only if that too fails.

decisions.summary: Ad-hoc dispatches not to a defined agent or adhoc-judge are counted per arm; opus ones reported as judging at session effort
decisions.why: Reports control failures honestly per US2 AS3/FR-012. Classifying by model is a heuristic; listing every such dispatch with its description would let the reader check it (aside, not a ruling).

decisions.summary: Sources ledger and page cache snapshotted once; each run gets its own copy through L7R_SOURCES_HOME; winner's ledger lines appended at landing
decisions.why: Removes the order advantage US2 AS6 and the edge case worry about; cache hits still counted per run.

decisions.summary: Claims file: launcher appends a release line after each R run, or a per-run copy if the rules do not read it so
decisions.why: Keeps the second R run from seeing the question as claimed; same starting state for both arms.

decisions.summary: make reserve collisions accepted as numbering gaps; shared state handled in research.md, with no run-record field listing what each run found at start or wrote outside its clone
decisions.why: Accepting the reserve gap is fine, but US2 AS6 and the shared-resource edge case require the RUN LOG to list what a run writes outside its clone that a later run reads and what each run found there at start. The claims release line and the reserve counter are exactly such writes. data-model's Run record carries env only; add a shared_state field (snapshot hash, claims lines, reserved prefixes).

decisions.summary: Task R is two page sessions (write, check-and-apply) from two pre-written byte-identical briefs, launched by the runner at the arm effort, with no orchestrating top-level session
decisions.why: FR-004 says one prompt file per task, but the spec's own FR-002/FR-003 put task R through write and check-and-apply sessions, which the project's runner takes as two briefs; each is a top-level headless session at the arm effort, which is the handoff's preferred form. The purpose (byte-identical, effort-free prompts) holds.

decisions.summary: effort-run: fresh clone of /diagram reset to START under neutral id diagram-exp-<id>, refuses while another run is live or rubrics/prompts changed, task I as one full claude -p with the interactive appended prompt, bypassPermissions, session ids chosen up front
decisions.why: FR-003, FR-005 (sequential, same start, same hooks), the neutral-id edge case.

decisions.summary: Exit 137 marks a run void from result.json and it is relaunched under the next id

effort-measure folds usage per message id as the census does, cross-checks result.json, reads rework from guard log, subagent transcripts, make results and git log; heuristic matches listed; usage-limit unobserved unless the GM reads it

effort-blind exports outputs, strips run id, clone path, session names, trailers and arm names, labels A/B from a seed, bundle outside the repo, key in the session clone's .git, committed after grades
effort-grader: opus, effort high, omitClaudeMd, Read/Grep, bundle only, registered in the tier table; GM grades the same bundle
Rubrics 0-4 anchored, weighted, pass line; committed before the first run; the launcher refuses if they changed since the freeze commit
Task I prompt names Inashiro as the reference and requires perf bookends and a worktree baseline
decisions.why: The project's standing rules for any generator change; identical across arms and silent on effort (FR-004).

decisions.summary: R winner lands after its in-run checks; I winner merged onto current main with make done and moved-map reviews there, defects recorded; losers deleted; future-work closed; report through escalation-check
